summary: Binary dropper executes on require — downloads and runs remote platform-specific payload
details: Package is advertised as an ESLint configuration but ships no such code. On module load, index.js require()s setup.js, which schedules a bootstrap via process.nextTick that selects a platform-specific asset (/pkg/package, /pkg/package-arm64, /pkg/loader_mac, /pkg/package.exe), fetches it from CDN hosts assembled at runtime from split-string arrays (oob-worker.cf99-9b3.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf100-416.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf101-adf.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf102-baf.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf103-070.workers.dev, tin.dl.well1.site, tina.dl.well1.site, ldr.dl.well1.site, win.dl.well1.site), stages the binary to /var/tmp or %TEMP%, chmods 0755, and executes it via child_process. Sensitive APIs and hostnames are hidden by string concatenation (os["plat"+"form"], os["user"+"Info"], fs["chmod"+"Sync"], require("child_"+"process")) to defeat static analysis. A SHA-256 fingerprint of hostname, username, cwd, node version and pid is sent as installId to the same CDN, so the installer's host identity reaches the attacker even when the binary fetch fails. The destination domains do not match the declared package purpose; the fetched binary is unpinned and unhashed.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
